cons: Only useful within Khan Academy's curriculum
Pedagogical approach frustrates students who want a direct answer
name: Khanmigo (Khan Academy)
pros: Safety and pedagogy designed in, not bolted on
COPPA and FERPA compliance built from the start
Tutors rather than answers, which serves learning outcomes
files: Khan Academy's curriculum content and student progress data.
value: A Socratic tutor that helps rather than answers, with content moderation and safety guardrails designed for minors from the ground up. Positioned against the risk of a student using a general assistant to skip the thinking rather than do it.
engine: Built on frontier models (primarily OpenAI) with Khan Academy's educational methodology and safety layer.
quality: Pedagogically oriented: better at guiding a student to an answer than at producing one efficiently. That is the intention.
tagline: The AI tutor Khan Academy built with child safety and learning theory at the centre.
use_cases: Guided tutoring on Khan Academy's curriculum without direct answer provision
Safe AI assistance for K-12 students in a moderated environment
Teacher-facing features for lesson planning and student progress context
governance_note: This is the reference case for child-safe AI deployment. The governance requirements for AI tools used by children are substantively different from adult deployment: COPPA (under 13), FERPA (student records), and the content moderation requirements that come with minors as users all apply. The product was designed with those constraints as requirements rather than afterthoughts. Institutions deploying any AI tool to K-12 students should use this as the comparison baseline for what a compliant product looks like.
training_optout: Follows OpenAI's sub-processor terms plus Khan Academy's own student data terms. COPPA and FERPA compliance are explicit product requirements.
